events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The complaint filed by the rider is an allegation of dangerous driving — speeding, hard braking throughout, overtaking on the shoulder — with the rider stating she was scared [F1][F3], and it is carried with the complete, fully timestamped two-message chat slice [F5]. A case of this type admits no automatic disposal: allegations of dangerous driving must go to a human reviewer [SAFE-2], and where the record raises threats, intimidation, harassment or abuse of any kind the same is true [SAFE-1]. I therefore screen the whole file before anything else and find no threat, insult, intimidation or sexual remark directed at either party: the chat is purely logistical — the rider's pickup note in a red cap [F3] and the driver's "4 min away, blue Toyota Prius" [F4] — and the driver's post-trip statement [F6] contains no hostility; only the riding-conduct allegation engages SAFE-2. On that basis the safety concern is recorded as suspected, not confirmed, and the case is escalated rather than decided.

The safety screen is as far as the record lets me go. The rider's account of speed, braking and shoulder use is a first-hand sensory claim but is corroborated by no system record; the only system data are aggregate, not event-level: actual distance 8.3 km against an optimal 8.4 km (−0.1 km) [F1] and duration 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate [F2]. Neither a shorter total distance [F1] nor a slightly faster-than-estimate completion [F2] can exclude a brief burst of speeding or a single hard-brake event, so neither fact confirms nor refutes the allegation, and the driver's "I drove normally" [F6] is a post-trip conclusion that, under the system-record-first rule, cannot outweigh the rider's account by itself. The gap is a missing record, not a point for either side: there is no speed trace, no harsh-event or g-force fact, no shoulder-use observation and no traffic fact in the file. Missing evidence must never be read as favouring either party, so the record cannot settle the dangerous-driving element and the case goes to a person [SAFE-2].

The route-deviation and fare branches are not engaged and produce no monetary remedy on these facts. RD-1 treats each off-route segment as a segment requiring review, but there is no off-route segment here — the driven path is 0.1 km shorter than optimal [F1] — so no segment falls under RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5. RD-2 attaches a refund to the extra kilometres of unexempted segments on a metered trip; with no extra kilometres [F1] no amount is computable, and in any event this was a non-metered RydeX trip charged at the fixed quoted fare of $20.85, which a fixed quote does not vary with mileage [RD-2]. FARE-1 leaves a non-metered fare standing where the fare equals the quote plus published surcharges, and no fact in this file records any surcharge, waiting fee, cancellation fee or added item, so no FARE-1 deduction arises. Both advocates concede this branch, and I accept it: the fare stands as charged and no refund, waiver or partial amount is entered, amount is therefore null [FARE-1][RD-2].

One further point the reviewer should see, though it needs an already-upheld route dispute to make it operative: the driver's profile carries 0 disputes and 0 upheld findings in 90 days [F8], so RD-6's condition — an upheld deviation in the last 90 days plus this case making it repeated — is not met, and no account action is recommended. The rider's profile [F7] likewise decides nothing on its own. I note, as both advocates did, that the complete chat contains no in-trip objection [F3][F4][F5], but silence during a ride is not consent to unsafe driving and does not establish consent to anything under RD-5; it is simply the absence of a contemporaneous complaint, which the reviewer may weigh as one circumstance among others.

ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human safety reviewer; do not execute any refund or fare change; hold the fixed $20.85 RydeX fare as charged pending review; ask the reviewer to weigh the rider's first-hand account against the absence of telemetry, and note the 995 / driver commercial insurance / RydeHELP reporting path to the rider. No account action on this record.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint states that the driver was speeding, braked hard throughout and overtook on the shoulder, and that the rider was scared and felt unsafe — this is an allegation of dangerous driving on the record.

The chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped) and contains no message in which the rider consented to any rerouting, speeding or shoulder overtaking; the only messages are the rider's pickup note and the driver's arrival note.

The driver's written statement ('I drove normally. The rider was on the phone the whole trip and never complained') is a bare after-the-trip assertion; it is denied by the rider's complaint and is not corroborated by any system record, and a passenger's failure to complain mid-trip is no consent to dangerous driving.
No traffic or weather fact exists for this trip, so nothing on the record explains or excuses abrupt braking, speeding or shoulder use as a response to road conditions.

The GPS record shows the route was not the problem (8.3 km actual vs 8.4 km optimal, i.e. -0.1 km) and the trip finished inside the estimate (12.7 min vs 13.8 min), so the safety complaint stands on the manner of driving rather than on distance or delay — and a met-ETA trip is consistent with aggressive driving rather than disproving it.

weaknesses: The complaint is uncorroborated by any system record: there is no telematics/accelerometer fact, no speed fact and no traffic fact in the table (F1, F2 only give distance and duration), so the speeding/braking allegation rests on the rider's own account, which under the system-record rule may be treated as weaker than the GPS/timeline data.

F2 (12.7 min actual vs 13.8 min estimated) and F1 (-0.1 km vs optimal) can be read by the driver as evidence of normal, non-erratic driving, and F6 (driver statement 'I drove normally') supports that reading; I cannot point to any record of a hard-braking or speeding event to rebut it.

The chat record (F3, F4, F5) contains no complaint during the trip, which the driver will use (F6) to argue the rider raised nothing at the time; the rider's own profile (F7) shows 0 disputes in 90 days, so there is no pattern of unfounded complaints either way.
No accident, injury or medical fact appears in the record, so the SAFE-2 escalation is grounded only on the allegation of dangerous driving rather than on any documented harm.

claims.assertion: The complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation ("speeding", "braking hard", "overtaking on the shoulder", "I was scared"), so this dispute must go to a human reviewer rather than any automatic outcome; I ask the judge to record the safety concern and escalate.

No system record supports the speeding or hard-braking narrative: the GPS track shows the trip finished in 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate (F2), i.e. slightly quicker than the quoted plan, and no GPS, timeline, traffic or fare fact in this file records abnormal acceleration, braking or shoulder use.

There is no route-deviation component to this dispute at all: actual distance was 8.3 km against an optimal 8.4 km (F1), a 0.1 km (-1%) shortfall, so no off-route segment and no excess mileage exists and nothing in RD-2 can be charged to the driver.

The fare was the fixed RydeX quote of $20.85 and no fact in this file contains any fare, waiting-fee, cancellation-fee or add-on component, so no monetary refund or fee waiver is computable from any fact and the fare should stand.

The rider raised no objection during the trip: the only messages before and during the ride are the rider's pick-up note and the driver's four-minute ETA reply (F3, F4), and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F5), so no in-trip complaint or request to slow down exists in the record.

The driver's own account is consistent with the system records: he states he drove normally and that the rider was on the phone throughout and never complained (F6), which matches the uneventful, on-time, on-distance GPS trace (F1, F2).

The driver has no history that would justify any account action: 963 trips in 90 days, rating 4.85, zero disputes and zero upheld findings in 90 days (F8), so a flag_account request would not be supported on this record.

weaknesses: The complaint is first-hand sensory evidence of speed, braking and shoulder overtaking (the rider's words in the complaint, indexed with the chat facts), and no fact in this file affirmatively disproves it — F2 shows only an aggregate duration 1.1 min under estimate, which cannot rule out a brief burst of speeding or a single hard-brake event.

The record contains no telemetry beyond route distance and duration (F1, F2): there is no speed trace, no harsh-event or g-force fact, so the driver cannot positively prove a safe driving style, only that nothing in the system data corroborates the allegation.

The driver's statement (F6) is a self-serving post-trip account and, per the system-records-first rule, carries little weight on its own; the rider's 3.3-year, 4.6-rated account with zero prior disputes (F7) is not the profile of a vexatious complainant, so a reviewer may treat the complaint as sincere.

Because this is classified as a safety case, the likely outcome is escalation rather than a clean no_action, so the driver's exposure is an open human review of his account rather than a dismissal of the complaint.

points.response: Conceded in direction, not in framing: I agree the case goes to a person under SAFE-2, but the record to hand the reviewer is the rider's complaint of speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking with the rider scared (F3, F5), which is an allegation of dangerous driving, not a mere slow-down request; the driver's 'never complained' point (F6) does not answer it.

Not contested that no telemetry fact exists, but F2 is an aggregate duration only (12.7 min vs 13.8 min estimate) and cannot exclude a brief burst of speeding or a single hard-brake event; F1 gives distance, not speed, so neither fact disproves the allegation — it is simply uncorroborated, which is why the human reviewer must weigh the rider's first-hand account under SAFE-2.

Agreed and irrelevant to my case: the rider claims no detour and asks for no mileage refund; F1's -0.1 km shows the safety complaint is about the manner of driving, so RD-1/RD-2 have no bearing and the driver cannot use a clean route to answer a driving-style allegation.

Agreed that no monetary remedy is computable from the facts (no fare facts exist in this file) and I request no refund, fee waiver or fare change; the fixed $20.85 RydeX fare and the account-review question are separate matters under SAFE-2.

The silence cuts both ways: F5 confirms the record is complete with every message timestamped, yet the only messages are the pickup note and the driver's ETA reply (F3, F4) — an unsafe passenger may well stay silent out of fear, and in any event F5 records no rider message consenting to speeding, hard braking or shoulder overtaking, so nothing in the chat legitimises the driving complained of.

F6 is the driver's own post-trip statement, and the system-record rule makes it the weakest item on the file; 'I drove normally' is a conclusion, not a record, and the uneventful aggregate in F1/F2 says nothing about acceleration, braking or shoulder use, so F6 cannot be weighed against the rider's F3/F5 complaint as if it were corroboration.

I do not seek flag_account on this record and F8 does not show the zero history the driver asserts — it shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days for him, which equally fails to rebut the rider's account and leaves the safety question for the human reviewer under SAFE-2; F7 shows the rider is a 3.3-year, 4.6-rated account with 0 prior disputes, not a vexatious complainant.

Withdrawn as framed rather than as fact: F1 and F2 correctly record an on-distance (-0.1 km) and under-estimate (12.7 vs 13.8 min) trip, but I no longer rely on them for any safety inference, since the manner-of-driving issue cannot be settled by aggregate distance and duration in either direction.

Accepted in the sense that the complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation and I do not resist escalation; note only that the words 'speeding / hard braking / shoulder overtaking / scared' live in the complaint narrative carried with the chat slice (F3, F5), and SAFE-2 routing to a human is the right disposal — not a finding of fault.

I agree with the reading of the exchange: the complete, fully timestamped two-message chat (F3, F4, F5) contains no reroute request and no consent to any route change — but that cuts for me, because F1 shows the actual route was 8.3 km against an 8.4 km optimal, so there was nothing to consent to and no deviation to excuse under RD-5.

I do not rest the case on F6 alone; I rest it on F1 and F2, which are system records showing the trip done in 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate over a route 0.1 km shorter than optimal, and a rider's silence mid-trip is offered only as absence of any contemporaneous objection (F3, F4, F5), not as consent to anything.

The absence of a traffic fact is neutral here rather than adverse: RD-4 only shifts an unexcused departure onto the driver when a gps-detour segment exists, and with actual distance 0.1 km below optimal (F1) there is no segment for RD-4 to operate on.

Their own claim concedes the only system data in the file (F1, F2) is consistent with an ordinary trip, and RD-2 requires an extra_km figure to produce any refund — with -0.1 km (F1) and no fare fact at all, no amount is computable, so the fare of $20.85 must stand and the case should go to a reviewer rather than to any refund.
